## Pull request overview

This pull request updates ObjectUI's filter handling to comply with ObjectStack Protocol v0.1.2+ by converting MongoDB-like filter operators to FilterNode AST format. The implementation introduces filter conversion utilities and updates both the core ObjectStackAdapter and the ObjectQLDataSource to use this new filter format.

**Changes:**
- Added filter-converter utility modules with MongoDB-to-AST conversion logic
- Updated ObjectStackAdapter and ObjectQLDataSource to convert filters before sending to the server
- Added comprehensive test coverage for filter conversion in the core package
- Updated documentation to explain the filter conversion and supported operators

The documentation example shows using `$regex` with a pattern `'^John'`, but the implementation converts regex patterns to simple substring matching using the `'contains'` operator. This is misleading because the regex anchor `^` (start of string) will be treated as a literal character in the substring match, not as a regex pattern.

Consider either:
1. Updating this example to use `$startswith` instead: `name: { $startswith: 'John' }` which accurately reflects the intended behavior
2. Adding a warning note that regex patterns are not fully supported and anchors/special characters will be treated literally

The filter-converter utility is duplicated across two packages (packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts and packages/data-objectql/src/utils/filter-converter.ts). This violates the principle of having a single source of truth and creates maintenance burden.

According to the ObjectUI architecture guidelines (Rule #5: Type Safety over Magic), there should be a central registry and shared types. The FilterNode type and conversion utilities should be defined in one location, preferably in the @object-ui/types package, and reused by both packages.

Recommendation: Move the FilterNode type definition to @object-ui/types and create a single implementation of the filter converter utilities that can be imported by both @object-ui/core and @object-ui/data-objectql packages.

The filter-converter utility tests are only present in the @object-ui/core package. Since the same utility exists in @object-ui/data-objectql, it should have its own test coverage as well, or the duplication should be eliminated by making data-objectql depend on core for this utility.

Currently, there's no test file at packages/data-objectql/src/utils/__tests__/filter-converter.test.ts to verify the behavior of the duplicated code in this package.
